items.title: Ida Goodson Interview, 1961-05-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I think I'll be around Micah. I think I'll be around Micah. I'll be around Micah, I believe.

ctx.x: No. I know she was a student teacher, because I remember one time she said that they had this program, and she played for some school there. It wasn't here, though. Somewhere else. And she said that she sang a solo on it, and by playing it, she won the top prize on that particular song. I can't remember the song now. I remember my mother telling you that. I don't know where about somewhere else. I've been in Georgia. I don't know where about somewhere else. I've been in Georgia. Well, she was birthed in Georgia.
She was birthed in Georgia? Yeah. What part of Georgia? I don't know where she was born there. I think I'll be around Micah. I think I'll be around Micah. I'll be around Micah, I believe.

Her part of Georgia. But her mother died when she was childbirth, and her grandmother taken her and brought her to Florida baby when she was in the home, you see, when she was raised there, but she wasn't right there. Do you remember her name before she married? Who? She's a White. She's a White. She's a White. She was a White.
